title: Graphs of quadratic functions and their properties
summary: Read the direction, turning point, axis of symmetry and intercepts of a parabola, and connect these features to the coefficients and forms of its quadratic rule.
objectives: Use the sign of a to determine whether a quadratic graph opens upward or downward.
Identify the maximum or minimum point and the vertical axis of symmetry.
Use roots, symmetric points and completed-square form to locate key graph features.

sections.title: The sign of a controls the opening

blocks.text: Every graph of y=ax²+bx+c with a non-zero is a parabola. If a is positive, the arms rise and the turning point is a minimum. If a is negative, the arms fall and the turning point is a maximum. A larger absolute value of a usually produces a narrower curve, while a value of |a| between 0 and 1 produces a wider curve.
The sign tells you the direction, but it does not by itself locate the turning point. The b and c terms can shift the graph horizontally and vertically.

sections.title: Turning point and axis of symmetry

blocks.text: The turning point is the lowest or highest point of the parabola. A vertical line through it is the axis of symmetry: reflected points on the curve have equal y-values. In completed-square form y=a(x-h)²+k, the turning point is (h,k) and the axis of symmetry is x=h.
Watch the sign inside the bracket. In (x-3)² the horizontal coordinate is 3, while in (x+3)² it is -3. The sign outside the bracket is not copied directly.

The y-intercept is found by setting x=0, so it is (0,c) in standard form. The x-intercepts, also called roots, occur where y=0. If two roots are r₁ and r₂, the axis of symmetry lies halfway between them.

Once the axis is known, any plotted point has a partner the same horizontal distance on the other side. This provides a fast graph check and can supply missing table values without repeating the full substitution.

sections.title: Read a quadratic in completed-square form

prompt.text: For y=-2(x-3)²+8, state the opening direction, turning point, axis of symmetry and maximum value.

content.text: The leading multiplier is -2, so the graph opens downward and has a maximum.
The turning point is (3,8), the axis is x=3, and the maximum value of y is 8.

sections.verification_note: At x=3 the squared term is zero, giving y=8; every other input makes -2(x-3)² non-positive, so no larger y-value is possible.

sections.title: Use roots to locate the axis and turning point

prompt.text: The function y=x²-6x+5 has roots 1 and 5. Find its axis of symmetry and minimum point.

content.text: Average the two roots to obtain the axis.
Since a=1 is positive, the graph opens upward. Its minimum point is (3,-4).

sections.verification_note: The roots are equally spaced two units from x=3, and y=(x-3)²-4 confirms the same minimum point.

prompt.text: A quadratic has roots x=-2 and x=8. What is the x-coordinate of its axis of symmetry?

feedback.text: The axis lies halfway between the roots: (-2+8)/2=3.

blocks.text: Use the sign of a for the opening direction, and describe the turning point as a minimum when a>0 or a maximum when a<0.
Read (h,k) from y=a(x-h)²+k, find the y-intercept from x=0, and use the midpoint of two roots to locate the axis of symmetry.

assets.alt_text: Side-by-side quadratic graphs showing that positive a gives an upward-opening curve with a minimum and negative a gives a downward-opening curve with a maximum.
